transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?
Hello. For the last few weeks I’ve just been on this intense high, like I’m wired all the time and can’t turn it off, and it’s starting to scare people at work.
Have you had any hallucinations, like hearing voices or seeing things others don’t, or any strong beliefs that other people say are not true?

Lately, when I'm working late, I've been hearing this deep male voice behind my left ear telling me I was "chosen" for this, though it sometimes turns harsh and says everyone would be better off without me if I screw up. I've also truly believed that I'm operating on a completely different level than everyone else and am the only one who can see the big picture. None of this ever happened before; it only started once I hit this intense high with the project launch.
Have you ever had a similar episode before, especially a period of feeling unusually high, needing very little sleep, or becoming overly energetic for several days or longer?

No, I really don't recall ever having an episode quite like this before, at least nothing this extreme. I've had busy times at work in the past, but nothing where I felt this completely wired and out of control.

Have you ever had any earlier episodes of feeling unusually high, needing very little sleep, or being much more energetic than usual that lasted several days or longer, even if they were milder than this one?

No, I don't recall ever having episodes of feeling that unusually high, energetic, or sleepless in the past. I have definitely experienced periods of really low mood before, but nothing like this revved-up feeling.
Have you ever had a period of several days or longer when you felt very depressed, lost interest in things, or had low energy or hopelessness that might suggest a prior mood episode?

Yes, for about three months now—actually starting just before this intense high hit—I've been stuck in this heavy, gray feeling of total hopelessness. I've completely lost interest in things I used to love, like weekend hikes and my side projects, and I just feel like there's no point because I've already ruined everything.
How long has this intense high, decreased need for sleep, and feeling wired been going on continuously? Has it lasted at least one week?
Yes, it's definitely been longer than a week. This intense high and feeling wired has been going on continuously for the last few weeks now. It just hasn't let up at all during this time.
Do the voice and beliefs only happen when your mood is very high or depressed, or do they ever continue when your mood feels normal?

The voice and those intense beliefs only happen when I'm in that highly revved-up, manic state. I've never heard anything like that or felt disconnected from reality when my mood is normal, or even during my low periods.
Do the voice and strong beliefs ever continue for at least two weeks when your mood is not unusually high or depressed, or do they only happen during those mood episodes?

No, they definitely don't continue when my mood is normal; they only happen during those intense high episodes. I have never heard that voice or felt disconnected from reality when my mood was stable or even during my low periods.
Have you ever had hallucinations or very strong false beliefs for at least two weeks when your mood was not unusually high or depressed?

No, I have never experienced anything like that when my mood was normal or stable. The voice and those beliefs only started during this recent intense high, and they have never happened during my past low periods either.
During your low periods, did you ever have hallucinations or fixed false beliefs for at least 2 weeks when you were not also feeling unusually high or energized?

No, I've never experienced anything like that during my low periods. The voice only happens when I am in that highly energized, manic state. When I'm down or feeling normal, I have never heard voices or felt disconnected from reality.
During your depressed periods, have you had thoughts of death or suicide, or ever tried to hurt yourself?

On my really dark days, I catch myself thinking it would just be simpler if I didn't wake up. I've had these flashes of standing at the edge of the train platform during my commute and wondering what it would be like to step forward. I haven't actually made any plans to do it, though, and I've never tried to hurt myself.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview is most consistent with bipolar I disorder, current episode manic with psychotic symptoms. He has a sustained manic syndrome lasting several weeks with elevated/expansive mood, feeling wired, reduced need for sleep/overactivity implied, grandiosity, and clear hallucinations/delusional beliefs that occur only during the manic state. He also reports a prior depressive episode lasting about 3 months, supporting bipolar I rather than a purely manic episode. Psychotic symptoms are mood-congruent and confined to the mood episode, which supports F31.2.
